clue.text: Trio outside commercial pub not having a nap

indicators.note: the trio's word sits outside, wrapping around the two words that follow it

blocks.note: a trio is three
a commercial is an advert, AD for short
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: Three people outside an advertised pub who have stayed up without a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: The nap here is not a snooze but the raised pile on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn-out fabric has lost its raised fibrous pile, the soft surface layer called the nap.

clue.text: Feature of the ocean even sounded out

indicators.note: sounded out asks us to say the word for even and hear another word

blocks.note: even, as in a level score, is tied

explanation.surface: Something notable about the sea that is even voiced out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: The regular rise and fall of sea water, pulled by the moon, is a defining characteristic of oceans.

clue.text: Artist with sense drinking my bitter

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing inside it

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist
nous is common sense
my! and cor! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A sensible painter knocking back a pint of my bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'. Bitter looks like the beer in a pub but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous describes deep-seated resentment, the same sour feeling as being bitter towards someone.

clue.text: Running arms — tradition for runner?

indicators.note: running here means in disarray or on the move, so the letters will not stay put

blocks.note: the two words supply all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: Is carrying weapons a custom for an athlete in a race?
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is not an athlete but someone who runs an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who manages or directs an organisation is said to run it, making the manager a runner.

clue.text: Journalists probing dullard’s issue when lying a lot

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so the journalists go into the next word

blocks.note: a dullard is a bore
editors, abbreviated EDS

explanation.surface: Reporters dig into a dim person's story about habitual dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying here means lying in bed, not telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer forming on skin pressed for long periods by bedding is a medical problem from staying recumbent.

clue.text: Upsets conductor on back of bus

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British orchestral conductor
the last letter of bus

explanation.surface: A bus conductor gets flustered at the rear of the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bus conductor collecting fares, but the conductor is Simon Rattle of the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve or disconcert them, which is what upsetting a person does.

clue.text: Add screening about to show nasty film

indicators.note: a screen shields something behind it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: to add is to sum
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A cinema adds a screening of an unpleasant movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The film is a layer on a liquid, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of dirt or froth forming on a liquid's surface is an unpleasant coating.

clue.text: What people believe in left-leaning business circles

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all the way round it

blocks.note: CO is short for company
left-wing politics is called red

explanation.surface: The convictions held among socialist-minded corporate circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a statement of faith or set of principles a person holds true.

clue.text: Spy alternative option for Hamlet? One’s expectant

blocks.note: M is the spymaster in the James Bond stories
an alternative is an other
Hamlet weighs 'to be, or not to be'

explanation.surface: Choosing between a spy and some other choice for Shakespeare's prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant woman is expecting a baby, so she is said to be expectant.

clue.text: Material dug up the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way up means the word is read from its end

blocks.note: dug, as in excavated, is mined

explanation.surface: Fabric that someone has excavated in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the sturdy cotton twill cloth used for jeans, a fabric.

clue.text: Energy cut in depressed region, creating damage

indicators.note: in places the first pair of words inside what follows

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy
to cut is to trim
a dent is a pushed-in area

explanation.surface: Energy cuts in an economically depressed area cause harm.
explanation.walkthrough: The depressed region sounds economic but is a physical hollow in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or loss suffered, so it means the same as damage.

clue.text: In case of trouble, stopping PC is clearly right

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
stopping a gap means plugging it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
PC is a police constable
the outside letters of trouble

explanation.surface: In an emergency, blocking a police officer is plainly justified.
explanation.walkthrough: PC is the British abbreviation for a police constable, an ordinary officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute or challenge is obviously correct, impossible to argue against.

clue.text: Breaking law, go on conceding this is a mistake

definitions.note: the whole phrase describes the answer: an error that concedes a goal

indicators.note: breaking smashes the words apart so they can be reassembled

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A player breaks the rules and keeps going, admitting the error.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the ball into your own net hands the opponents a goal, a football blunder.

clue.text: Old lady suggesting executed English monarch?

blocks.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles
the executed Charles was Charles the First

explanation.surface: An elderly woman who brings to mind a beheaded king.
explanation.walkthrough: CR ONE reads as Charles Rex the First, Charles I, beheaded in 1649.
explanation.definitionFit: A crone is a withered old woman, often in folklore, so an elderly female.

clue.text: Pleasant crossing ring road that’s not too steep

indicators.note: to cross something is to go across it, so the outer word spans the inner

blocks.note: pleasant and friendly
a ring is O-shaped
RD is short for road

explanation.surface: A gentle slope on a friendly ring road that is not too steep.
explanation.walkthrough: Steep here means expensive, not sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: A price within one's means is reasonable, and a steep price is an excessive one.

clue.text: Flirting from flipping coquette is too forward

indicators.note: from says the letters come straight out of the words that follow
flipping turns the run of letters back to front

blocks.note: a run of letters across the end of coquette and the next words

explanation.surface: Flirtatious behaviour from a flighty coquette who is too bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a game of touching feet under the table is a classic flirtatious move.

clue.text: Small paper and grass skirts something seen on star

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edges

blocks.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
S is short for small
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A tiny newspaper and grass skirts worn by a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: SUN and POT together skirt S. The star is the astronomical kind, not a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark patches appear on the surface of the sun, which is itself a star.

clue.text: Training period of rifle carrying finished

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside

blocks.note: to rifle is to ransack or plunder
time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: A stint of instruction in handling a gun, now completed.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifle is a verb meaning plunder here, not a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupillage is the year a trainee barrister spends learning under a qualified one.

clue.text: Inferior and under the weather, dropping out

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away, removing it

blocks.note: feeling unwell is being out of sorts
taken as written; this word is the one removed

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly and below par, someone quits a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as 'a meal of sorts' is a poor, second-rate example of its kind.

clue.text: Char wraps a short time for part of course

indicators.note: wrapping something goes all around it

blocks.note: to char is to scorch or sear
a minute, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Cooking where a burnt crust forms briefly, as one stage of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is an academic one, not a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small discussion class forming one element of a university course.

clue.text: Place to drink tea, say, turned up by bishop

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word that follows is read backwards

blocks.note: tea is an example of a brew
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric arrives at a café to sip tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewpub is a bar brewing its own beer on site, a venue for drinking.

clue.text: British drive forwards and flourish

blocks.note: B is short for British
to urge on is to drive forwards

explanation.surface: Britain pushes ahead and thrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow rapidly and thrive, so it shares the sense of to flourish.

clue.text: Wander round, heading for Dubrovnik and Split

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Dubrovnik
a split is a rift

explanation.surface: A traveller roams around Croatia, heading for Dubrovnik and Split.
explanation.walkthrough: Split looks like the Croatian city alongside Dubrovnik, but it means a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift is to move about aimlessly, which is to wander around.

clue.text: Northerner‘s short stay in French hotel?

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, losing a final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a stay in a hotel is counted in nights
no letters: it places the stay in France, asking for the French word for night

explanation.surface: A northern traveller's brief stay at a hotel in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word for night is nuit, and a night is the unit of a hotel stay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous people of the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.

clue.text: Military delaying time of a match

indicators.note: delaying something holds it back until later, so it leaves its place and comes further on

blocks.note: martial means military
T is short for time

explanation.surface: The army holding up the start time of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of MARTIAL is moved two places later. The match is a marriage, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a match between two people, and marital means relating to marriage.

clue.text: One’s admired swimming area with lake at the bottom

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom is the end, so this letter goes last

blocks.note: a lido is an open-air swimming pool
L is short for lake

explanation.surface: A popular bathing spot with a lake at the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: LIDO already holds an L; it moves from the top to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person greatly loved or revered by fans, someone others look up to.

clue.text: Supposedly conservative style of rebel in US, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many that the letters could take

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Is a traditional fashion really the look of an American rebel?
explanation.walkthrough: A blue rinse is a bluish hair tint linked with older women, and blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinted hairdo is a stereotype of older, traditional voters, hence a supposedly Tory look.

clue.text: Directors craving a change of scene, we’re told

indicators.note: we are told means we hear it spoken rather than see it written

blocks.note: someone wanting a change of scene is fed up

explanation.surface: Company executives longing for somewhere new.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's directors sit together as a governing body, collectively called its board.

clue.text: Fare from Asia, say, moving south

indicators.note: moving south sends a letter downward, to the end of the word

blocks.note: Asia is an example of the East
S is short for south

explanation.surface: Food from the Orient travelling southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of EAST moves to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, and fare is the food served at a meal.

clue.text: With old English ex-PM touring, called for zest

indicators.note: touring goes all around a place, enclosing it

blocks.note: OE is the abbreviation for Old English
called on the phone
Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: A former prime minister on tour, summoned for his enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Zest is the citrus rind, not enthusiasm, so the definition is a fruit word.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the outer coloured rind of a citrus fruit, grated for flavour in cooking.
